cards.text: Jethro, the priest of Midian, is the father-in-law of Moses, Israel's leader. He hears about all that God has done for Moses and His people Israel, and how the LORD brought Israel out of Egypt. Friend, news like that does NOT stay quiet.
Earlier, Moses had sent back his wife Zipporah, and Jethro had taken her in, along with her two sons. Two boys, and Moses gave each one a name with a reason behind it.

cards.question: Moses' first son is named Gershom. What reason had Moses given for that name?

answers.text: He had been a foreigner in a foreign land
He had been drawn out of the water
He had found rest in a new home

cards.question: True or false: Moses named his other son Eliezer because the God of his father delivered him from the sword of Pharaoh.

cards.text: Jethro comes with Moses' wife and sons to the desert, where Moses is camped at the mountain of God, and he sends word ahead: "I, your father-in-law Jethro, am coming to you with your wife and her two sons." A father-in-law who calls BEFORE he shows up? Friend, that's RARE.

cards.question: The message reaches Moses. What does Moses do when his father-in-law Jethro arrives?

answers.text: He bows down and kisses him
He sends Joshua to meet him
He waits for him in the tent

cards.text: They greet each other and go into the tent. Then Moses tells Jethro all that the LORD did to Pharaoh and the Egyptians for Israel's sake, and I bet that visit did NOT wrap up early.

cards.question: True or false: When Moses tells Jethro the story, he shares only the good parts and skips the hardships along the way.
Jethro has heard how the LORD rescued Israel from the Egyptians. How does Jethro respond?

answers.text: He rejoices over the good the LORD did
He worries about the road ahead
He asks Moses to come back home

cards.text: Jethro declares, "Blessed be the LORD, who has delivered you from the hand of the Egyptians and of Pharaoh, and who has delivered the people from the hand of the Egyptians." The priest of Midian, blessing the LORD out loud, and friend, he is just getting warmed up.

cards.question: After hearing all of it, Jethro says that now he knows the LORD is ___ than all other gods.

cards.text: Then Jethro brings a burnt offering and sacrifices to God. And he doesn't eat alone.

cards.question: Who comes to eat bread with Jethro in the presence of God?

answers.text: Aaron and all the elders of Israel
Joshua and all his fighting men
Hur and the leaders of Midian

cards.text: The next day Moses takes his seat to judge the people, and they stand around him from morning until evening. MORNING until EVENING, friend? That's not a line, that's a lifestyle.

cards.question: Jethro sees everything Moses is doing for the people. What does he ask Moses?

answers.text: Why Moses sits alone as judge
Why the people argue so much

cards.question: Moses answers his father-in-law. Why does Moses say the people come to him?

cards.text: Whenever the people have a dispute, it comes to Moses to judge between one man and another. And he makes known to them the statutes and laws of God.
Jethro doesn't soften it one bit: "What you are doing is not good." Whoo. Friend, I've heard that about my blurry old stamps, and it STINGS.

cards.question: Why does Jethro say what Moses is doing is not good?

answers.text: The task is too heavy for him alone
The laws are too hard to explain
The people keep ignoring his rulings

cards.text: Now Jethro has some advice for Moses, and he adds, "may God be with you." First, Moses must be the people's representative before God and bring their causes to Him.

cards.question: True or false: Jethro tells Moses to hand off teaching God's statutes and laws to someone else.

cards.text: Then comes the big piece of the plan: select capable men from among the people. And Jethro is VERY specific about who makes the cut.

cards.question: What kind of men does Jethro tell Moses to choose as leaders?
Jethro says to appoint these men over the people as leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties and of ___.

cards.text: These leaders will judge the people at all times. Moses won't be the only judge in the camp anymore.

cards.question: Under Jethro's plan, which cases do the new leaders bring to Moses?

cards.text: The minor cases they can judge on their own, so Moses' load gets lightened as they share it with him. I once tried to fill every cookie box by myself, friend, and I am STILL recovering.

cards.question: If Moses follows this advice and God so directs him, what does Jethro say will happen?

answers.text: Moses will endure and the people go home in peace
Moses will finally get to return to Midian
The people will never have a dispute again

cards.text: Moses listens to his father-in-law and does everything he says. He chooses capable men from all Israel and makes them leaders of thousands, of hundreds, of fifties and of tens.

cards.question: True or false: The new leaders bring the difficult cases to Moses and judge the minor ones themselves.
With the new leaders judging the people, what happens with Jethro?

answers.text: He returns to his own land
He stays and travels with Israel
He becomes a leader of thousands

findings.problem: The card says Moses gave each son a name with a reason behind it. That covers the naming in verse 4 (Eliezer) as well as verse 3, but the card cites only Exodus 18:2-3. It should cite Exodus 18:2-4.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This is not the opening card, but it has three sentences: the arrival and message, then "A father-in-law who calls BEFORE he shows up?", then "Friend, that's RARE."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The reason Jethro gives in verse 11, "for He did this when they treated Israel with arrogance," is never told on any card. It is the reason behind his confession that the LORD is greater than all other gods.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Aaron first appears in the passage at verse 12, but the baker only meets him inside the right answer ("Aaron and all the elders of Israel"), so he is never introduced as Moses' brother. Joshua and Hur also appear only in wrong answers, without introductions.
findings.question: When a person first appears only inside an answer, does the rule to say who they are still apply? If it does, should the introduction go on an earlier story card, even if that card would then hint at the answer?

findings.problem: This is not the walkthrough's opening card, but it has three sentences: the judging scene, "MORNING until EVENING, friend?", and "That's not a line, that's a lifestyle."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Why Aaron isn't judging too" is close in meaning to the right answer "Why Moses sits alone as judge." Asking why no one else is judging is a way of asking why Moses judges alone, so a baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke "I've heard that about my blurry old stamps" adds a new moment to the backstory, in which someone told him his stamps were not good. The backstory says the opposite: "Mother Miller never complained." The moment is set in the Millers' kitchen, not his bakery, so the allowance for made-up bakery moments doesn't cover it.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the last item in a list they haven't seen ("thousands, of hundreds, of fifties and of ___"). This tests unseen wording, not meaning the baker can reason out.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The setup line "Moses won't be the only judge in the camp anymore" rules out the wrong answer "Every case in the camp" on card 13. That leaves only two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
